answer: Anchor each identity to a hardware enclave: an agent must present a remote attestation proving its code runs inside a distinct trusted execution environment before it can earn. One enclave key yields one identity, and the key cannot be copied or shared. A sybil operator therefore has to buy real hardware for every fake — like tending a garden where each plant needs its own plot of soil, not a whisper of code copied a thousand times. When attested capacity approaches its zenith, the network raises the attestation bond, so mass fakery gets priced out by physics, not policy.
